candidates.statement: Second, the initial production ratio of the neighboring nuclides $^{238}$U and $^{232}$Th should be far less sensitive to variations in the poorly-known characteristics of the neutron exposure(s) occurring in the explosion of progenitor than the ratios of nuclides more widely separated in mass, such as $^{232}$Th and $^{151-153}$Eu (Goriely & Clerbaux [@goriely99]).

However, the computed actinide production ratios should be veriﬁed by observations of daughter elements such as Pb and Bi in the same star, which are independent of the subsequent history of star formation and nucelosynthesis in the Galaxy.
